newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 3rd wk in row.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 3rd wk in row.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell a third consecutive week during the week ending June 20, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgages fell 11 basis points to an average 7.61 percent, the lowest since a rate of 7.56 percent in the week ended February 21, 1997. Last week's 30-year rate averaged 7.72 percent.
Fifteen-year mortgages fell 13 basis points to 7.14 percent from 7.27 percent, the lowest since a rate of 7.06 percent in the February 21 week.

One-year adjustable rate mortgages dipped to an average 5.66 percent from 5.67 percent last week. Freddie Mac said the ARM has not been lower since it stood at 5.61 percent in the week ended March 14, 1997.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.30 percent, the 15-year 7.81 percent and the ARM 5.93 percent.

"Retail sales and housing starts were both down in May, indicating a moderation of economic growth in the second quarter. Complementing this, the Producer Price Index was down three-tenths of a percent as well," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said in a statement.
"Given this evidence of slower growth and very low inflation, our outlook is for a continued affordable housing market," Nothaft said.
Also earlier this week the Labor Department reported a 0.1 percent rise in U.S. May consumer prices.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.5 percent on ARM loans, also unchanged from the previous week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
